features.name: Original public problem catalog
features.behavior: Three original tasks; case-folded search, difficulty/tag filters, bounded pagination, samples/starters/hints and provenance; no private grading data.
features.limits: In-memory fixed seed catalog, not authoring/import/search infrastructure.

features.name: Fixed-JWKS account token verification
features.behavior: Exactly one bounded Bearer header, fixed EdDSA/Ed25519 key source, no jku/x5u/crit redirection, bounded keys/body, cached rotation, strict issuer/audience/use/lifetime/subject.
features.limits: No API token revocation callback; valid issued tokens can survive web logout until their maximum five-minute expiry.

features.name: Owned durable submissions and history
features.behavior: SQLite WAL state, UUID idempotency scoped per user, payload conflict checks, 32 KiB UTF-8 source limit, one active attempt/account, ten attempts/minute/account, 100 active global queue bound, owned history/source access and generic verdict summaries.
features.limits: Source never executes in API. Local persistence lacks production retention/encryption/backups/deletion. Expiration is lazy on queue/history operations.

features.name: Trusted judge worker protocol
features.behavior: Dedicated bearer trust, runtime/language allowlist, current heartbeat requirement, transactionally exclusive leases, per-job random hashed lease tokens, expiry and one-shot bounded completion; public summaries ignore worker-controlled summary text.
features.limits: API trusts authenticated controller preflight assertion; actual isolation is owned by services/judge, not attested by API itself.

features.name: Versioned offline authored hint contract
features.behavior: Authenticated fixed-catalog requests with integer levels 1-3, extra fields forbidden, public-only future provider context, bounded response/provenance validation, three-second request timeout, safe failures.
features.limits: No live model, generated tutoring/solver loop or provider API key. Browser currently uses catalog-authored hints directly.

features.name: Bounded bodies and non-reflecting API errors
features.behavior: 128 KiB body cap, ten-second receive timeout, generated request IDs, nosniff and stable public 4xx/5xx payloads without reflecting private/internal text.
features.limits: No substitute for aggregate ingress limits or redacted operational observability.

features.name: Locked Python API runtime and nonroot container
features.behavior: Five exact runtime package pins, two exact dev tools, SHA-256 artifact lock, optional managed CA mounted at build time, nonroot runtime and ignored private state.
features.limits: This review did not run installation/build/audit or assert current dependency advisory status.

security_findings.title: Configured JWKS URL permits HTTP on non-loopback hosts

evidence.observation: Server configuration selects JWKS URL; URL validation permits either http or https for any hostname. Token headers cannot select this destination.

security_findings.impact: A deployment using cleartext JWKS over an untrusted network would let an on-path party substitute the verification key and forge account tokens. This is conditional on deployment configuration/network trust, not an observed local bypass. Internal Compose routing intentionally uses HTTP.
security_findings.recommendation: Document and enforce production trust requirements: use HTTPS for external JWKS or an explicitly trusted internal route, preserving supported local/Compose behavior.

security_findings.title: Submission source/history has no retention or deletion lifecycle

evidence.observation: Schema durably stores user ID and full source code.
Rate and queue limits bound new/active work, but completed records are retained without a cumulative storage cap.
Owned history is readable but no deletion/retention operation is present.

security_findings.impact: Over sustained use, private code and identifiers persist indefinitely and database storage grows without a code-level bound. File mode 0600 and ownership filtering do not supply production encryption, deletion policy or backups.
security_findings.recommendation: Before public operation define consent, retention/deletion, source-size/cumulative storage budgets, tested backup/restore and operational access controls.

security_findings.title: General API concurrency/request quotas and future model quotas are absent

evidence.observation: Each request has a 128 KiB size bound and ten-second receive bound.
Public catalog/health/capabilities and authenticated hints have no application-wide request limiter.
Submission-specific active-work/rate/global queue limits do exist.

security_findings.impact: Individual request bounds do not bound aggregate simultaneous connections or cheap request floods. Current hints are authored and do not incur model cost; real provider quotas remain a future prerequisite.
security_findings.recommendation: Use bounded ingress/concurrency and appropriate account/network quotas in a production deployment; add cost/token budgets only when implementing a real provider.

security_findings.title: API trusts one shared configured worker bearer token without independent strength validation

evidence.observation: Worker control requires a nonempty shared token compared in constant time; API itself does not enforce minimum token entropy or per-worker identity.
Any authenticated worker may register/select worker IDs under the shared trust domain.

security_findings.impact: Weak manually configured tokens or a compromised trusted worker can expose the shared controller trust domain. Native launcher generation/validation is stronger, and leased job tokens still protect one-shot completion. No missing-auth bypass was found.
security_findings.recommendation: Keep worker control network-private, require high-entropy configuration, and consider rotation/per-worker authentication for production.

security_findings.title: JWKS stream has per-operation timeouts rather than a total fetch deadline

evidence.observation: HTTPX has connect/read/write/pool timeouts and a 64 KiB document cap, but no outer total-duration deadline around streaming.
Refresh holds a per-URL lock while awaiting the fetch.

security_findings.impact: A slow configured issuer or network can keep a refresh in progress substantially longer than five seconds by delivering chunks before each read timeout. This affects availability, not signature acceptance, and requires the configured destination/route to stall.
security_findings.recommendation: Consider an outer asyncio timeout covering the full JWKS fetch and a regression test using a slow chunked issuer.

security_findings.title: API interpreter and base image pins are broader than the root native version

evidence.observation: API project requests Python 3.12 rather than an exact patch.
Container uses mutable python:3.12-slim and pip-installed uv 0.13.6; frozen application dependencies follow.

security_findings.impact: Native patch selection and future container rebuild contents can differ even when uv.lock is unchanged. This is not evidence of a vulnerable installed package.
security_findings.recommendation: When strict reproducibility is required, align documented patch pins and choose a maintained digest-pinned image with an update policy.

security_findings.title: Protected endpoints do not declare a FastAPI bearer security scheme

evidence.observation: Bearer header is parsed manually from Request.
Protected route dependencies reference require_user rather than a FastAPI Security bearer declaration.

security_findings.impact: Generated OpenAPI does not describe authentication in a way Swagger Authorize understands; actual requests still enforce signatures. Existing schema tests only assert paths/models, not auth documentation.
security_findings.recommendation: If interactive authenticated docs are desired, declare the bearer security contract without weakening existing strict parsing and duplicate-header checks.

security_findings.title: History summaries fetch and construct full source details before dropping source

evidence.observation: List SELECT * materializes source_code for each row, builds SubmissionDetail, then converts to SubmissionSummary.

security_findings.impact: A 100-item summary page can read/process approximately 3.2 MiB of source unnecessarily. Ownership is preserved and source is excluded from the response.
security_findings.recommendation: For a measured large-history workload, select summary fields directly and keep the owned detail route separate.

security_findings.title: JWT tests stub the JWKS transport and do not exercise stream/document boundaries

evidence.observation: Issuer fixture replaces _fetch_jwks with an in-process function.
Transport failure/document tests replace the fetch function rather than exercising HTTPX content length/chunking/redirect behavior.

security_findings.impact: Tests cover signatures, parsing, caching and fail-closed decisions but do not prove the concrete HTTP transport enforces declared/streamed size and redirect constraints. Static inspection finds those controls implemented.
security_findings.recommendation: When changing JWKS transport, add focused HTTPX mock-transport tests for oversized streams, redirects and total timeout.

summary: No critical authentication/ownership/worker-secret bypass or host execution in the API identified by static review. Listed issues are explicit local-prototype limitations, configuration risks and focused future improvements, not reproduced vulnerabilities or a security certification.
boundaries: Only auth.py performs outbound HTTP, to the configured fixed JWKS URL; token-supplied destinations are rejected.
API stores source as text and passes it only to authenticated worker leases; no eval/exec/subprocess/Docker API is imported by API source.
Submission visibility is always selected by both account ID and job ID; worker ID/lease secrets are not public detail fields.
Private grading cases stay in services/judge; catalog/hint context contain original public statements and samples only.
SQLite path and JWKS URL are trusted runtime configuration, not request fields.
No model-provider dependency, model weights, GPU training code or paid inference is enabled in API.

duplicate_and_consolidation_candidates.recommendation: Optionally share a small signing-key/JWKS fixture in conftest.py when tests next change; preserve real signatures and each test isolation boundary.
An indexed catalog lookup helper could replace repeated linear scans if catalog scales; three seed problems do not justify a rewrite.
Keep the transactional create() recheck even though existing() duplicates it: it protects concurrent requests and the offline-worker retry path. Consolidate only error construction if useful.
Keep feature-specific model boundaries for now. Generate shared API client contracts when the frontend integration grows rather than merging unrelated modules.
No API file deletion/move justified: source modules are imported, tests provide meaningful security/behavior coverage and lock/config files support the workflow.
